note.text:
Digital rights management (DRM) is technology that controls how digital content (music, films, e-books, software, games) can be used, to protect copyright.
Examples:
• Licence keys and product activation for software.
• Streaming services that let you watch but not download, or only on registered devices.
• E-books that cannot be copied or printed; encrypted DVDs; region codes.
• Watermarks that identify the owner.
Advantages: protects creators' income, reduces piracy. Disadvantages: can stop fair uses, may need internet to check licences, content may become unusable if the service closes.

sections.heading: Protecting digital content
sections.text: Digital files can be copied perfectly in seconds. Digital rights management (DRM) is technology that controls how music, films, e-books, games and software may be used, so copyright holders are paid.

sections.heading: How DRM works
sections.text:
• Licence keys and activation: a code proves you bought the software.
• Streaming limits: watch or listen online, often without downloading, on a limited number of devices.
• Copy and print restrictions on e-books; encryption on DVDs; region codes.
• Watermarks: visible or hidden marks showing who owns or bought the content.

sections.heading: For and against
sections.text:
For: it reduces piracy and protects the income of musicians, film makers and programmers.
Against: it can stop honest uses (moving a song you bought to a new phone), may need the internet to check licences, and content can become unusable if the service closes.
Avoid 'cracked' software that removes DRM: it is illegal and often carries malware.

mistake.wrong: DRM makes content free to copy
mistake.why: Its purpose is to protect copyright.

worked_example.problem: Bih buys a film on a streaming app. She can watch it on her phone but cannot copy it to her friend's laptop. Why?
steps: The film is protected by DRM.
The licence allows viewing only on her registered account or device.
This stops unlicensed copies being shared.
worked_example.answer: DRM limits copying to protect the film's copyright

cards.idea: DRM controls how digital content can be used.
DRM protects creators but can limit users.
example: You may need the internet to activate software.

pick.q: Which is an advantage of DRM for a musician?
pick.r: It helps stop illegal copies, protecting income
w: It removes the need for a licence
e: It does not change the sound.

pick.q: Which is a disadvantage of DRM for users?
pick.r: Content may stop working if the service closes or there is no internet to check the licence

pick.q: Why do some people say DRM is too strict?
pick.r: It can stop legal uses, like moving a song you bought to a new device
pick.y: Strict controls can affect honest buyers.

cards.idea: A licence key proves software was paid for.
example: A code typed in during installation

pick.r: Technology that controls how digital content can be used and copied
w: A way to make files bigger
e: It protects content; it is not malware.

pick.q: What is the main purpose of DRM?
pick.r: to protect copyright and reduce piracy
pick.y: Creators control how their work is used.

pick.q: A code must be typed in before a program can be used.
w: a strong password for your e-mail
e: Region codes limit where discs play.
That protects an account, not a product licence.
pick.y: The key proves the copy is licensed.

pick.q: A faint logo is printed across a photo.
e: Region codes restrict playback by region.

pick.q: An e-book can be read in its app but cannot be copied or printed.
e: A backup is a copy, the opposite.

e: It does not change the sound.

pick.q: A friend offers a 'cracked' version of a paid game that removes the licence check. What should you do?
pick.r: Refuse: it breaks copyright and may contain malware
e: Free does not make it legal.
pick.y: Cracked software is illegal and risky.

pick.q: Why do streaming apps limit the number of devices per account?
pick.r: To stop one paid account being shared by many people
pick.y: The licence is for the subscriber.

pick.q: Which is a fair balance between creators and users?
pick.r: Paying for content while having reasonable rights to use what you bought
w: Users have no rights at all
pick.y: Both creators' and users' interests matter.
